# Partial leakage as a lattice of feedback channels

Version 0.1 — 2026-10-12. Exact fixtures for the gap named in
[evaluation_feedback_insertions.md](evaluation_feedback_insertions.md) §H:
feedback that reveals failure *categories* and not items. Module
`src/spiral_ln/evaluation_feedback_lattice.py`; tests
`tests/test_evaluation_feedback_lattice.py`; receipt
`output/evaluation_feedback_lattice/lattice_v0_1.json`. No model was called.
Evidence levels are those of the calculus card (§11): *algebraic identity*
(a proof for all inputs), *finite verified example* (checked on the enumerated
cases only), *synthetic mechanism result* (none here).

```powershell
$env:PYTHONPATH = "src"
python scripts/verify_evaluation_feedback_lattice.py --output output/evaluation_feedback_lattice/lattice_v0_1.json
python -m pytest tests/test_evaluation_feedback_lattice.py -q
```

## 1. Channels are partitions; the lattice data-processing law

A deterministic feedback channel on outcome records \(\{0,1\}^n\) is a function
\(f\). Two channels transmit the same information exactly when they have the
same kernel partition \(\ker f\), so a channel *is* a partition of the record
set. Convention: \(p\le q\) when \(q\) refines \(p\); the one-block partition
(`sealed`) is the bottom, the discrete partition (`item_level`) is the top,
\(p\vee q\) is the common refinement (observing both), and \(p\wedge q\) is the
finest common coarsening (components of the union of the two relations). This
is the partition lattice with its usual orientation reversed.

**Proposition 1 (lattice data-processing law and converse).** For all
distributions \(P,Q\) on records, \(p\le q\) implies
\(\mathrm{TV}(p_\#P,p_\#Q)\le\mathrm{TV}(q_\#P,q_\#Q)\). Conversely, if
\(p\not\le q\) there are point masses \(P,Q\) with the inequality reversed.

*Proof.* \(\mathrm{TV}(p_\#P,p_\#Q)=\max_U|P(U)-Q(U)|\) over unions \(U\) of
blocks of \(p\). When \(q\) refines \(p\), every block of \(p\) is a union of
blocks of \(q\), so the maximum for \(p\) ranges over a subset of the sets
available to \(q\). If \(q\) does not refine \(p\), some block of \(q\) holds
\(x,y\) in different blocks of \(p\); \(P=\delta_x,Q=\delta_y\) give
\(\mathrm{TV}\) one through \(p\) and zero through \(q\). \(\square\)

Hence \(\mathrm{TV}\) through \(p\vee q\) is at least the larger of the two and
through \(p\wedge q\) at most the smaller. The one-kernel contraction in the
testbed is the special case of a single comparable pair.
*Evidence status: algebraic identity.* Fixture `lattice_fixture(2, 2)`: all 15
partitions of \(\{0,1\}^2\), 225 ordered pairs, 100 pairs of grid
distributions; the law holds on every comparable pair, fails somewhere on every
non-comparable pair, join/meet meet their lattice definitions, and
`access_kernel`'s three classes are recovered as bottom, middle, top.

## 2. Category leakage is an order embedding, not a scale

A category map on items, a partition \(\gamma\) of \([n]\), induces the channel
\(\Phi(\gamma)\): the per-category pass-count vector.

**Proposition 2.** \(\Phi(\gamma)\le\Phi(\gamma')\) iff \(\gamma\le\gamma'\)
(\(\Phi\) is an order embedding); \(\Phi(\text{one block})=\)`score_only` and
\(\Phi(\text{singletons})=\)`item_level`.

*Proof.* If \(\gamma'\) refines \(\gamma\), each \(\gamma\)-count is a sum of
\(\gamma'\)-counts, so equal \(\gamma'\)-counts force equal \(\gamma\)-counts.
If not, some \(\gamma'\)-block holds items \(i,j\) that \(\gamma\) separates;
the records failing only \(i\) and only \(j\) have equal \(\gamma'\)-counts and
unequal \(\gamma\)-counts. The endpoints are the definitions. \(\square\)
*Evidence status: algebraic identity*, checked exhaustively on all 5 maps of
\([3]\) and 15 maps of \([4]\) in `category_order_fixture`.

Because the image is order-isomorphic to the partition lattice of \([n]\), which
is not a chain for \(n\ge3\), "how much leaks" has no scalar. Fixture: on
\([3]\), \(A=\{0,1\}|\{2\}\) and \(B=\{0\}|\{1,2\}\); \(B\) separates
"fail item 0" from "fail item 1" (\(\mathrm{TV}=1\)) while \(A\) does not
(\(0\)); \(A\) separates "fail 1" from "fail 2" while \(B\) does not.

**Finite observation.** \(\Phi\) does not preserve joins: for rows
\(\{0,1\}|\{2,3\}\) and columns \(\{0,2\}|\{1,3\}\),
\(\Phi(\gamma\vee\gamma')\) is `item_level` but
\(\Phi(\gamma)\vee\Phi(\gamma')\) confuses `1001` with `0110` (equal row and
column sums). Two separate category leaks are strictly coarser than one leak
with the refined categories: 219 of 225 ordered pairs on \([4]\) preserve the
join, 225 of 225 preserve the meet. *Evidence status: finite verified example*
(the join failure is a proof by witness; meet preservation is checked, not
proven).

## 3. Cost of a leak, exact

Setting of `noise_ceiling_fixture`: clean accuracy \(4/5\), flip \(1/10\), so
observed accuracy \(v=37/50\), ceiling \(9/10\); on \(n=50\) items, 13 fail and
\(H=8\) hits are needed. Under \(\Phi(\gamma)\) the loop knows
\((n_c,F_c)\) per category and patches uniformly at random without replacement
inside a category; a patch on a passed item gains nothing.

**Proposition 3 (expected gain is exact; greedy is optimal).** The \(j\)-th
patch in category \(c\) hits with conditional probability
\((F_c-h)/(n_c-j+1)\) given \(h\) earlier hits, and with unconditional
probability \(F_c/n_c\) for every \(j\) (exchangeability). So \(m_c\) patches
hit \(m_cF_c/n_c\) in expectation, exactly; the expected-value formula of the
insertions note is the hypergeometric mean, not an approximation. Since every
patch in \(c\) has the same marginal value, filling categories in decreasing
order of \(F_c/n_c\) maximizes expected hits at every patch count.
*Algebraic identity*; the module checks the greedy optimum against every
allocation and the per-patch rate against every patch order.

**Proposition 4 (patches to the ceiling).** Let \(c_1,c_2,\dots\) be the greedy
order, \(j\) the first index with \(\sum_{i\le j}F_{c_i}\ge H\),
\(N_{<j}=\sum_{i<j}n_{c_i}\), \(H_j=H-\sum_{i<j}F_{c_i}\in[1,F_{c_j}]\). The
expected score reaches the ceiling at
\(m^*=N_{<j}+H_jn_{c_j}/F_{c_j}\); the realized score first reaches it at a
stopping time \(T\) with \(\mathbb E[T]=N_{<j}+H_j(n_{c_j}+1)/(F_{c_j}+1)\)
(negative-hypergeometric mean; the categories before \(c_j\) are patched
completely, so their hit counts are deterministic). Hence
\(m^*-\mathbb E[T]=H_j(n_{c_j}-F_{c_j})/(F_{c_j}(F_{c_j}+1))\in[0,m^*/(F_{c_j}+1))\):
the expected-score crossing never understates the expected patch count.
With one category, \(m^*/n=(1-\varepsilon-v)/(1-v)=8/13\) and
\(\mathbb E[T]=8\cdot51/14=204/7\); with singleton categories both equal
\(H\), share \(4/25\). *Algebraic identity*, cross-checked against enumeration
of every patch order on three category shapes and against
`ceiling_detection_threshold` / `targeted_ceiling_detection_threshold`.

**Proposition 5 (monotonicity of \(m^*\)).** If \(\gamma'\) refines \(\gamma\)
then \(m^*(\gamma')\le m^*(\gamma)\) for every failure pattern. *Proof.* Each
\(\gamma\)-rate is the size-weighted mean of its \(\gamma'\)-sub-rates, so the
expected-hit curve of \(\gamma\) is attainable under \(\gamma'\) by
proportional (fractional) allocation, and the \(\gamma'\)-greedy curve is at
least it. \(\square\) *Algebraic identity*; checked over all 203 maps of
\([6]\), 2268 refining pairs, 63 patterns, two requirements each.

**Finite observations on the realized stopping time.** \(\mathbb E[T]\) under
the static greedy schedule is *not* monotone along refinement: one block
\((4,2)\), \(H=2\), gives \(10/3\), while \((2,1),(2,1)\) gives \(7/2\); on
\([6]\) a witness is record `001101`, \(H=3\), \(21/4\) against \(11/2\). An
adaptive schedule that re-queries the channel after every patch and patches
the highest current rate (solved exactly by dynamic programming on count
multisets) was at most the static value in every enumerated case and monotone
on every refining pair of \([6]\) and along the 50-item chain; no proof is
offered. 50-item chain, block sizes 50, 25, 10, 5, 2, 1 with failures at items
\(0,4,\dots,48\): \(m^*/n = 8/13, 7/12, 8/15, 1/2, 8/25, 4/25\);
\(\mathbb E[T]_{\text{static}} = 204/7, 201/7, 51/2, 23, 31/2, 8\);
\(\mathbb E[T]_{\text{adaptive}} \approx 29.14, 25.64, 21.17, 18, 12, 8\).
*Evidence status: finite verified example.*

## 4. Ledger wrapper

`audit_category_ledger` accepts a `category_feedback` event carrying the
partition used, records it with its position (`score_only`, `category`,
`item_level`), and forwards to `audit_ledger` one `score_query` per block of
two or more items and one `item_feedback` naming the singleton items, since a
count on a singleton is that item's outcome. The base access rules then apply;
an optional declared partition per set bounds the leak in the lattice and a
finer event is a recorded breach. `audit_ledger` is wrapped, not edited.

## Boundaries

Deterministic channels only. A stochastic channel is a Markov kernel; the
\(\mathrm{TV}\) contraction survives (`_pushforward`), but a kernel has no
partition, the lattice and the converse of Proposition 1 do not apply, and the
Blackwell preorder on kernels is not treated. Items independent; a patch
changes its own item only, which the nearest-neighbour learner in
`output/eval_reuse_toys` violated. Ties in the greedy order are broken by
index, and \(\mathbb E[T]_{\text{static}}\) depends on that choice when two
categories share a rate. Nothing here is evidence about any model or loop.

# Partial leakage as a lattice of feedback channels

Version 0.1 — 2026-10-12. Exact fixtures for the gap named in
[evaluation_feedback_insertions.md](evaluation_feedback_insertions.md) §H:
feedback that reveals failure *categories* and not items. Module
`src/spiral_ln/evaluation_feedback_lattice.py`; tests
`tests/test_evaluation_feedback_lattice.py`; receipt
`output/evaluation_feedback_lattice/lattice_v0_1.json`. No model was called.
Evidence levels follow the calculus card (§11): *algebraic identity* (proved
for all inputs), *finite verified example* (checked on the enumerated cases
only). No synthetic mechanism result is claimed.

```powershell
$env:PYTHONPATH = "src"
python scripts/verify_evaluation_feedback_lattice.py --output output/evaluation_feedback_lattice/lattice_v0_1.json
python -m pytest tests/test_evaluation_feedback_lattice.py -q
```

## 1. Channels are partitions; the lattice data-processing law

A deterministic feedback channel on records \(\{0,1\}^n\) is a function \(f\);
two channels carry the same information exactly when \(\ker f\) agrees, so a
channel *is* a partition of the record set. Convention: \(p\le q\) when \(q\)
refines \(p\); the one-block partition (`sealed`) is the bottom, the discrete
partition (`item_level`) the top, \(p\vee q\) the common refinement (observing
both) and \(p\wedge q\) the finest common coarsening (components of the union
of the two relations). This is the partition lattice, orientation reversed.

**Proposition 1 (lattice data-processing law and converse).** For all
distributions \(P,Q\) on records, \(p\le q\) implies
\(\mathrm{TV}(p_\#P,p_\#Q)\le\mathrm{TV}(q_\#P,q_\#Q)\); and if \(p\not\le q\)
there are point masses \(P,Q\) reversing the inequality.

*Proof.* \(\mathrm{TV}(p_\#P,p_\#Q)=\max_U|P(U)-Q(U)|\) over unions \(U\) of
blocks of \(p\). When \(q\) refines \(p\), every block of \(p\) is a union of
blocks of \(q\), so the maximum for \(p\) ranges over a subset of the sets
available to \(q\). If \(q\) does not refine \(p\), some block of \(q\) holds
\(x,y\) that \(p\) separates; \(P=\delta_x,Q=\delta_y\) give \(\mathrm{TV}\)
one through \(p\) and zero through \(q\). \(\square\)

So \(\mathrm{TV}\) through \(p\vee q\) is at least the larger of the two and
through \(p\wedge q\) at most the smaller; the testbed's one-kernel contraction
is one comparable pair. *Evidence status: algebraic identity.* Fixture
`lattice_fixture(2, 2)`: all 15 partitions of \(\{0,1\}^2\), 225 ordered pairs,
100 pairs of grid distributions; the law holds on every comparable pair, fails
somewhere on every non-comparable pair, join and meet satisfy their lattice
definitions, and `access_kernel`'s three classes are bottom, middle, top.

## 2. Category leakage is an order embedding, not a scale

A category map, a partition \(\gamma\) of the items \([n]\), induces the channel
\(\Phi(\gamma)\): the per-category pass-count vector.

**Proposition 2.** \(\Phi(\gamma)\le\Phi(\gamma')\) iff \(\gamma\le\gamma'\),
so \(\Phi\) is an order embedding; \(\Phi(\text{one block})=\)`score_only` and
\(\Phi(\text{singletons})=\)`item_level`.

*Proof.* If \(\gamma'\) refines \(\gamma\), each \(\gamma\)-count is a sum of
\(\gamma'\)-counts, so equal \(\gamma'\)-counts force equal \(\gamma\)-counts.
If not, some \(\gamma'\)-block holds items \(i,j\) that \(\gamma\) separates;
the records failing only \(i\) and only \(j\) have equal \(\gamma'\)-counts and
unequal \(\gamma\)-counts. The endpoints are the definitions. \(\square\)
*Evidence status: algebraic identity*, checked exhaustively on all 5 maps of
\([3]\) and 15 maps of \([4]\) in `category_order_fixture`.

The image is order-isomorphic to the partition lattice of \([n]\), not a chain
for \(n\ge3\), so "how much leaks" has no scalar. Fixture on \([3]\):
\(A=\{0,1\}|\{2\}\), \(B=\{0\}|\{1,2\}\). \(B\) separates "fail item 0" from
"fail item 1" (\(\mathrm{TV}=1\)) while \(A\) does not (\(0\)); \(A\) separates
"fail 1" from "fail 2" while \(B\) does not.

**Finite observation.** \(\Phi\) does not preserve joins: for rows
\(\{0,1\}|\{2,3\}\) and columns \(\{0,2\}|\{1,3\}\), \(\Phi(\gamma\vee\gamma')\)
is `item_level` but \(\Phi(\gamma)\vee\Phi(\gamma')\) confuses `1001` with
`0110` (equal row and column sums): two separate category leaks are strictly
coarser than one leak with the refined categories. On \([4]\), 219 of 225
ordered pairs preserve the join and 225 of 225 the meet. *Finite verified
example*: the join failure is proved by its witness; meet preservation is
checked, not proved.

## 3. Cost of a leak, exact

Setting of `noise_ceiling_fixture`: clean accuracy \(4/5\), flip \(1/10\), so
observed accuracy \(v=37/50\) and ceiling \(9/10\); on \(n=50\) items 13 fail
and \(H=8\) hits are needed. Under \(\Phi(\gamma)\) the loop knows
\((n_c,F_c)\) per category and patches uniformly at random without replacement
inside a category; a patch on a passed item gains nothing.

**Proposition 3 (expected gain is exact; greedy is optimal).** The \(j\)-th
patch in category \(c\) hits with conditional probability
\((F_c-h)/(n_c-j+1)\) given \(h\) earlier hits, and with unconditional
probability \(F_c/n_c\) for every \(j\) (exchangeability). So \(m_c\) patches
hit exactly \(m_cF_c/n_c\) in expectation: the expected-value formula of the
insertions note is the hypergeometric mean, not an approximation. Every patch
in \(c\) has the same marginal value, so filling categories in decreasing order
of \(F_c/n_c\) maximizes expected hits at every patch count. *Algebraic
identity*; checked against every allocation and every patch order.

**Proposition 4 (patches to the ceiling).** With \(c_1,c_2,\dots\) the greedy
order, \(j\) the first index with \(\sum_{i\le j}F_{c_i}\ge H\),
\(N_{<j}=\sum_{i<j}n_{c_i}\) and \(H_j=H-\sum_{i<j}F_{c_i}\in[1,F_{c_j}]\):
the expected score reaches the ceiling at \(m^*=N_{<j}+H_jn_{c_j}/F_{c_j}\),
and the realized score first reaches it at a stopping time \(T\) with
\(\mathbb E[T]=N_{<j}+H_j(n_{c_j}+1)/(F_{c_j}+1)\) (negative-hypergeometric
mean; earlier categories are patched completely, so their hits are
deterministic). Hence
\(m^*-\mathbb E[T]=H_j(n_{c_j}-F_{c_j})/(F_{c_j}(F_{c_j}+1))\in[0,m^*/(F_{c_j}+1))\):
the expected-score crossing never understates the expected patch count. One
category: \(m^*/n=(1-\varepsilon-v)/(1-v)=8/13\), \(\mathbb E[T]=204/7\).
Singleton categories: both equal \(H\), share \(4/25\). *Algebraic identity*,
cross-checked by enumerating every patch order on three category shapes and
against `ceiling_detection_threshold` and `targeted_ceiling_detection_threshold`.

**Proposition 5 (monotonicity of \(m^*\)).** If \(\gamma'\) refines \(\gamma\)
then \(m^*(\gamma')\le m^*(\gamma)\) for every failure pattern. *Proof.* Each
\(\gamma\)-rate is the size-weighted mean of its \(\gamma'\)-sub-rates, so the
\(\gamma\) expected-hit curve is attainable under \(\gamma'\) by proportional
(fractional) allocation, and the \(\gamma'\)-greedy curve is at least it.
\(\square\) *Algebraic identity*; checked over all 203 maps of \([6]\), 2268
refining pairs, 63 patterns, two requirements each.

**Finite observations on the stopping time.** \(\mathbb E[T]\) under the static
greedy schedule is *not* monotone along refinement: one block \((4,2)\), \(H=2\),
gives \(10/3\); \((2,1),(2,1)\) gives \(7/2\). On \([6]\): record `001101`,
\(H=3\), \(21/4\) against \(11/2\). An adaptive schedule that re-queries the
channel after each patch and patches the highest current rate (solved exactly
by dynamic programming on count multisets) was at most the static value in
every enumerated case and monotone on every refining pair of \([6]\) and along
the 50-item chain; no proof is offered. Chain with block sizes 50, 25, 10, 5,
2, 1 and failures at items \(0,4,\dots,48\):
\(m^*/n=8/13,7/12,8/15,1/2,8/25,4/25\);
\(\mathbb E[T]_{\text{static}}=204/7,201/7,51/2,23,31/2,8\);
\(\mathbb E[T]_{\text{adaptive}}\approx29.14,25.64,21.17,18,12,8\).
*Finite verified example.*

## 4. Ledger wrapper

`audit_category_ledger` accepts a `category_feedback` event carrying the
partition used, records it with its position (`score_only`, `category`,
`item_level`), and forwards to `audit_ledger` one `score_query` per block of
two or more items and one `item_feedback` naming the singleton items, since a
count on a singleton is that item's outcome. The base access rules then apply;
an optional declared partition per set bounds the leak in the lattice, and a
finer event is a recorded breach. `audit_ledger` is wrapped, not edited.

## Boundaries

Deterministic channels only: a stochastic channel is a Markov kernel, for which
the \(\mathrm{TV}\) contraction survives (`_pushforward`) but which has no
partition, no lattice position, and no converse of Proposition 1; the Blackwell
preorder on kernels is not treated. Items are independent and a patch changes
its own item only, which the nearest-neighbour learner in
`output/eval_reuse_toys` violated. Greedy ties break by index, and
\(\mathbb E[T]_{\text{static}}\) depends on that choice when two categories
share a rate. Nothing here is evidence about any model or loop.

Deliverables are in WT (all new files, no existing module edited; `git status --short` shows exactly these five untracked paths):

- `WT\src\spiral_ln\evaluation_feedback_lattice.py` (module, 885 lines, LF)
- `WT\tests\test_evaluation_feedback_lattice.py` (64 tests, all pass; combined run with `test_evaluation_game_feedback.py` = 94 passed; the testbed suite also still passes)
- `WT\scripts\verify_evaluation_feedback_lattice.py` (mirrors the feedback verifier; mode "x"; sha256 of itself, the new module, feedback and testbed)
- `WT\output\evaluation_feedback_lattice\lattice_v0_1.json` — `all_passed: true`, 19 checks, source hash matches the final module; CRLF like the other receipts
- `WT\paper\evaluation_feedback_lattice.md` (148 lines)

**Statements and their status**

Convention: `p <= q` iff `q` refines `p`; bottom = one block (sealed), top = discrete (item_level); join = common refinement, meet = finest common coarsening (components of the union of relations). The partition lattice with reversed orientation.

1. *Lattice data-processing law and converse* (algebraic identity, proved): `p <= q` implies `TV(p#P,p#Q) <= TV(q#P,q#Q)` for all P,Q, because TV of a pushforward is the max of |P(U)-Q(U)| over unions of blocks and the coarser channel's unions are a subset. Converse: if `p` is not below `q`, point masses on two records that `q` joins and `p` separates reverse it, so TV-domination for all P,Q *characterizes* the order. Checked for all 15 partitions of {0,1}^2, 225 ordered pairs, grid of 10 (fixture) / 20 (tests) distributions; join/meet verified against lattice definitions; `access_kernel`'s classes recovered as bottom, middle, top.

2. *Category map Φ is an order embedding* (algebraic identity, proved): Φ(γ) refines Φ(γ') iff γ refines γ'; Φ(one block)=score_only, Φ(singletons)=item_level. So the image is order-isomorphic to the partition lattice of [n], a partial order for n>=3: no scalar "amount of leak". Exhibit on [3]: A={0,1}|{2}, B={0}|{1,2}; B separates fail-0 from fail-1 (TV 1) while A gives 0; A separates fail-1 from fail-2 while B gives 0. Finite observation: Φ does not preserve joins (rows {0,1}|{2,3} and columns {0,2}|{1,3}: refined categories give item_level, the joint leak confuses 1001 with 0110) — proof by witness; 219/225 ordered pairs on [4] preserve joins, 225/225 preserve meets (meet preservation only checked, not proved).

3. *Cost of a leak* (fixture n=50, v=37/50, ceiling 9/10, 13 failures, H=8 hits).
   - The expected-value formula is exact, not an approximation: the j-th random patch in a category hits with conditional probability (F_c−h)/(n_c−j+1) and unconditional probability F_c/n_c for every j (hypergeometric mean), so greedy by F_c/n_c maximizes expected hits at every patch count (proved; checked against all allocations and all patch orders).
   - Expected-score crossing m* = N_<j + H_j·n_j/F_j; exact expected stopping time E[T_static] = N_<j + H_j(n_j+1)/(F_j+1) (negative hypergeometric); error m*−E[T] = H_j(n_j−F_j)/(F_j(F_j+1)) ∈ [0, m*/(F_j+1)) — all algebraic identities, cross-checked by enumerating every patch order. k=1: m*/n = 8/13 (= `ceiling_detection_threshold`), E[T]=204/7; k=n: 4/25 (= `targeted_ceiling_detection_threshold`), E[T]=8.
   - m* is monotone along refinement (proved via proportional fractional allocation; checked on all 203 maps of [6], 2268 refining pairs, 63 patterns × 2 requirements). 50-item chain (blocks 50,25,10,5,2,1): m*/n = 8/13, 7/12, 8/15, 1/2, 8/25, 4/25.
   - Finding: E[T_static] is **not** monotone: (4,2),H=2 gives 10/3 but the refinement (2,1),(2,1) gives 7/2; on [6] witness record 001101, H=3: 21/4 vs 11/2. An adaptive re-query greedy (exact DP on count multisets) was ≤ static everywhere and monotone on every enumerated pair and the chain (≈29.14, 25.64, 21.17, 18, 12, 8) — no proof offered.

4. *Ledger wrapper* `audit_category_ledger`: `CategoryFeedbackEvent` carries the partition; translated to one `score_query` per block ≥2 and one `item_feedback` on singleton items, so base access rules apply; optional declared partition per set, finer events recorded as breaches; partitions rendered in the report.

**Not settled**: meet preservation of Φ and adaptive-greedy monotonicity in general (finite checks only); E[T_static] depends on the index tie-break when categories share a rate (stated in the paper). Timing: verify ≈ 10–20 s depending on machine load (sibling processes were slowing everything 3×; I added a shared DP cache and integer-key sorting). Note: Python hangs under the Bash tool here; I used the PowerShell tool.
